assurance: Internal written terminal-mass proofs and exact bounded controls. Lemma 19 excludes stability of a fixed two-to-one projection under all complementary braids for even t>=4; Theorem 20 excludes all positive global polynomial DT orbit minima for odd N>=15 and proves extraction without a monodromy hypothesis. Pure-DT connectivity follows with the retained degree-thirteen base and two-leaf absorption; mixed connectivity remains open. No independent replay, formal verification or external review.

declarations.name: Lemma 1. Terminal mass detects exactly the removable locus
declarations.scope: For every polynomial DT tree on N=2r+1 sheets, lambda(A) is the sum of its two terminal-component sizes minus two. The minimum mu over all factors lies in [0,N-4] and is zero exactly when a DT has two exclusive leaves on different edges.

declarations.name: Lemma 2. Bringing another factor preserves a chosen cut
declarations.scope: For arbitrary factors A,B, move B unchanged toward A, using positive moves from the right or negative moves from the left. All three component sets after deleting A stay literal and connected; both selected factors are unchanged. The cost is their positional distance minus one.

declarations.name: Lemma 3. An outer one-contact gives strict descent
declarations.scope: If mu>0 and a minimizing DT A has support intersection exactly one with B at an outer endpoint a, cut-preserving bringing followed by conjugating B by A strictly reduces mu in at most r-1 ordinary moves. Stop at the first decrease to keep all preceding masses equal. The terminal mass drops by the size of the nonempty branch pruned from the a-component.

declarations.name: Lemma 4. Two degree-two contacts can create two new leaves
declarations.scope: For adjacent A=(ab)(cd),B=(ae)(cf) on six distinct labels, with every other factor fixing a,c, one inverse move produces ((be)(df),A). The two degree-two contacts become exclusive leaves of A; deleting them and A leaves a full-cycle polynomial tuple. Reverse the adjacent input order and use a positive move for the same retained A. No claim about arbitrary bringing preserving these degree conditions.

declarations.name: Lemma 5. Five weighted components control every adjacent-pair rotation
declarations.scope: For any adjacent DT pair, delete its four edges and record five positive component weights and the component of each support label. Every pair rotation has exactly the terminal masses computed on that weighted quotient tree. Q^k(A,B)=(A(AB)^k,A(AB)^(k+1)) and ord(AB) is in {2,3,4,5,6}. An endpoint mass inequality does not control intermediate masses or guarantee any descending pair exists.

declarations.name: Lemma 6. Seven weighted components control the complete three-factor orbit
declarations.scope: For every consecutive triple in a full-cycle polynomial DT tree, its six edges leave seven weighted components. Keep at most twelve literal support labels and their owner map. The complete local B3 orbit has at most 2205225 states independently of N. Each rotating factor mass is a 0/1 linear expression in the seven weights minus two; subset-minimal coefficient vectors suffice for every positive weighting.

declarations.name: Proposition 7. The plateau window has eight uniform inequalities
declarations.scope: The stated nine-label path-owner template has 162 local states and 27 terminal coefficient vectors, with exactly eight minimal supports. Its smallest candidate mass is min(alpha+beta,alpha+gamma,beta+gamma)-2, where alpha=min(w0,w1), beta=w3, gamma=min(w5,w6). Every original factor is uniformly strictly dominated. All 189 tree-quotient owner partitions of this fixed support forest exclude 387 of 567 marked templates; 180 have positive isolated linear witnesses with odd total weight. Other triple support forests and global completions are not classified.

declarations.name: Proposition 8. Orbit minima replace monotone descent
declarations.scope: Extraction in a fixed-degree braid orbit is equivalent to its minimum terminal mass being zero. At a positive orbit minimum m, every local candidate vector satisfies c.w>=m+2, and an initially minimizing factor satisfies equality. Any endpoint violation contradicts minimality regardless of intermediate masses. Three chosen factors including a minimizer can be gathered while preserving their literal permutations and the chosen cut; recompute seven-component data after gathering.

declarations.name: Lemma 9. Complementary twists develop the three cuts simultaneously
declarations.scope: A minimizing factor can be conjugated to the first position while retaining its literal cut sets. The complementary product is a full cycle on each set; its full twist simultaneously develops every complementary factor, preserving those sets and the minimum. Outer one-contacts are absent at every phase.

declarations.name: Theorem 10. Cyclic compatibility excludes closed terminal trees
declarations.scope: For every positive global minimum of a full-cycle polynomial DT braid orbit, front-place a minimizing A with cut sets S,M,U and complementary product R. Its restrictions are full cycles and simultaneous R-power conjugation of the complement retains the cuts and mass. The absence of outer one-contacts forces no terminal-internal DT, a common rooted cyclic matching for every SU pair, and at least one SM or UM pair. Each such pair satisfies ell<=2s and ell/gcd(s,ell)<=4 (or the U analogue). No full alternating monodromy assumption is needed.

declarations.name: Corollary 11. Positive minima have restricted mass and terminal sizes
declarations.scope: Every positive global orbit minimum m of a full-cycle polynomial DT tuple satisfies 3m>=N-4. Unequal nonsingleton terminal sizes at a minimizing factor are possible only for (s,u,ell)=(2,3,4) or (3,4,6), up to terminal swap, in degrees nine or thirteen. For N>=15 terminals therefore have equal sizes or a singleton. Sizes (1,t) force ell=t; ell=2t with 2|t; ell=3t/2 with 4|t; or ell=4t/3 with 6|t. Equal terminals force odd ell and ell/gcd(s,ell) in {1,3}. These are necessary conditions, not complete exclusion of full-alternating positive minima.

declarations.name: Lemma 12. Exact three- and four-phase covers align the endpoints
declarations.scope: For every terminal-middle contact at a positive global minimum, an order-three phase coset forces h and the middle edge difference to be g or 2g, and both terminal endpoint phases to agree modulo g. A common twist gives support intersection three. An order-four cover likewise forces the terminal endpoints to agree modulo g.

declarations.name: Corollary 13. Ratio three is excluded in the residual degree range
declarations.scope: At every minimizing factor of a positive global polynomial DT orbit minimum with N>=15, equal terminal sizes s>1 require odd ell dividing s. Singleton terminals (1,t), t>1, require ell=t or ell=2t with even t. Ratio three for equal terminals is excluded by two new minimizing pair-rotation endpoints and Corollary 11; singleton ratios 3/2 and 4/3 are excluded by simultaneous residue preservation along the terminal tree. No full alternating hypothesis or middle-middle attachment assumption is used.

declarations.name: Lemma 14. The tree support code has an exact invariance test
declarations.scope: The binary factor-support span for a polynomial DT tree has dimension r=(N-1)/2 and is invariant under its generated permutation group exactly when all pairwise support intersections are even. The incidence map of the expanded tree proves both directions; one-cut phase covers alone do not imply invariance.

declarations.name: Lemma 15. Equal-middle singleton cuts force a removable factor
declarations.scope: No minimizing factor at a positive global polynomial DT orbit minimum has terminal sizes (1,t) and middle size t for t>=3. Theorem 10 and all-factor mass inequalities force two paths with corresponding edge pairs. A closest neighboring-index pair can be gathered by commuting swaps; either capture sign creates a removable DT. No full alternating hypothesis is needed. At t=2 a five-state dihedral orbit has positive minimum one.

declarations.name: Corollary 16. The remaining positive-minimum cuts
declarations.scope: For N>=15 every minimizing factor at a positive global polynomial DT orbit minimum has equal terminal sizes s>1 and odd middle size ell dividing s, or terminal sizes (1,t) with middle size 2t and even t. These are necessary conditions; full-alternating exclusion remains open.

declarations.name: Theorem 17. Only the equality singleton family can remain
declarations.scope: At a tuple-minimizing factor A no other factor has one edge in each terminal component: its middle would be M_A plus two nonempty root sides, and lambda(B)<=lambda(A)-2. For positive global minima with N>=15, Corollary 16 therefore leaves only (1,t;2t), even t, N=3t+1 and m=(N-4)/3. Every polynomial DT orbit with N>=15 and N not congruent to 1 modulo 6 has a removable factor. No monodromy hypothesis is used.

declarations.name: Lemma 18. Saturated singleton covers force antipodal roots
declarations.scope: In the equality singleton family, for even t>=4 the middle roots differ by t in the complementary 2t-cycle. Saturated phase covers and the elementary noncrossing property of a reduced cycle factorization prove this. Every terminal-middle edge projects modulo t to its terminal partner, giving exactly the terminal tree. Its support intersection with the minimizer is zero or two at every phase; odd contacts with the minimizer can occur only at one middle label of a middle-middle factor. The natural antipodal matching is broken by terminal-middle generators; no global invariant code is established.

declarations.name: Lemma 19. Complementary braids cannot preserve a saturated projection
declarations.scope: For a polynomial DT tree with cuts (1,t;2t), even t>=4, t-1 terminal-middle and t/2 middle-middle factors, no fixed two-to-one projection M->U can make every terminal-middle edge project to its terminal partner after every complementary braid. Pair conjugations force a common lifted terminal tree, then fibrewise action of every middle-middle factor on its vertices; conjugating such a factor by a terminal-middle factor forces it to fix those vertices, contradicting middle connectivity.

declarations.name: Theorem 20. Every residual pure-DT orbit admits extraction
declarations.scope: For every polynomial DT braid orbit on odd N>=15 sheets the global minimum terminal mass is zero, with no monodromy hypothesis. Every orbit therefore has a removable two-leaf DT. The complete degree-thirteen base and canonical two-leaf absorption give absolute unmarked pure-DT connectivity for every residual degree; exact marking removal gives marked connectivity. Mixed connectivity remains separate.
